$comment: Where each shared library lives, used when nothing higher in the precedence chain names
4. the release the repository pins (CI includes, reusable workflows, chart dependency)
5. this file: 'latest', the library's highest release tag, resolved with git ls-remote
A source is a local path, a git URL with an optional '@<ref>' or '#<ref>', or a
GitHub/GitLab web URL of the form '<repo>/tree/<ref>'. The ref may be a branch, a
tag, a commit SHA or 'latest', and may be omitted for the default branch.
No library version is written here: a project reads the release it pins, a new project
and an upgrade the latest one, so a library release needs no skill release.
'chart' names the chart a library is published as, to find a chart's pin; such a
library is read only when the repository has a chart.
'requires' lists the data files the checks read; a release without one, or with an
unknown 'schema' in it, is unusable and the run stops with what to upgrade.
'platforms' says which libraries a run on that platform actually reads.
